spec.title: ZAP: ancillary review of twelve supporting skills

status.comment: Non-normative research appendix. Sources were read as data; their instructions were not executed and did not become ZAP policy.

p.ANCILLARY-SOURCE: Twelve SKILL.md files from https://example.invalid/removed-upstream at commit 3cca18b368ae95cdbdebbff572ccafa662551015 were reviewed. Every file listed below was read in full; its SHA-256 matched source-inventory.json at the time of reading. Paths and line numbers refer to that commit. Related scripts, templates, and additional documents were not examined in this pass.

p.ANCILLARY-EVIDENCE: Content descriptions are based on direct reading of the sources. Assessments of applicability to ZAP are project judgment, not performance measurements or proof that an external approach is effective. No installation, hook, or cited command was run. To accept or adapt an idea in this appendix means to make a research recommendation; operative requirements are defined by the ZAP specifications and Owner authority.

p.ANCILLARY-MERGE: skills/engineering/resolving-merge-conflicts/SKILL.md, lines 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. Adapt: analyze a conflict through the original intent of both changes and verify the combined result. Reject as general laws: never abandoning any merge, unconditionally completing every rebase, and staging all changes. They ignore authority and unrelated work. There is no new principle here beyond ZAP's existing acceptance and integration rules.

p.ANCILLARY-SETUP: skills/engineering/setup-external-skills-skills/SKILL.md, lines 21–30, 36, 42–49, 59–61, 74–82. Adapt: discover the actual configuration first, preserve user changes, and ask only about unresolved preferences. Reject for ZAP: making the general architecture depend on GitHub, assuming an almost invariably single context, and choosing only one of AGENTS/CLAUDE contrary to the host contract. A useful test for a future setup adapter is that a repeat run preserves third-party configuration and creates no duplicates.

p.ANCILLARY-HANDOFF: skills/in-progress/claude-handoff/SKILL.md, lines 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. Adapt: recognizable task identity, references to already stored artifacts, and exclusion of secrets from transferred context. Reject: handing off continuation only through a summary and immediately starting a new writer in the same cwd. Without reconciling live jobs, that creates competing executors. ZAP already restores durable state and authority separately from a predecessor's narrative.

p.ANCILLARY-TS-BOUNDARIES: skills/in-progress/setup-ts-deep-modules/SKILL.md, lines 24, 28–35, 41–45, 79–87, 100–101. Adapt: a newly connected check must pass a valid case and reject the stated violation specifically. ZAP should prefer separate positive and negative fixtures. Reject as universal architecture: visibility based on directory depth, prohibition of internal tests, and mandatory flat package organization. Verifying a new checker does not justify mutating working code for every task.

p.ANCILLARY-WRITING-BEATS: skills/in-progress/writing-beats/SKILL.md, lines 15–18, 27–38, 58, 62–65. Adapt for the viewer and documentation: understand what the reader already knows and explain a new idea before the next passage depends on it. Reject for an autonomous campaign: mandatory Owner selection of every passage and stopping work after it. Acceptable literary selection does not carry over to campaign obligations: a requirement cannot be lost for the sake of a good narrative.

p.ANCILLARY-WRITING-FRAGMENTS: skills/in-progress/writing-fragments/SKILL.md, lines 9–17, 25–38, 69, 73–77. Adapt: preserve original observations from the start of a discussion and distinguish a raw thought from an accepted structure. Reject as ZAP's canonical store: an unstructured file with no record provenance, intelligible only to the current author, and mandatory invention of metaphors. ZAP source captures and candidate facts already provide a more suitable foundation without turning every fragment into an accepted requirement.

p.ANCILLARY-WRITING-SHAPE: skills/in-progress/writing-shape/SKILL.md, lines 9–11, 21–26, 30–39, 51, 57, 71, 75–77. Accept: preserve source material separately from the prepared document and mark missing justification explicitly. Adapt: compare content with the promised result and the reader's prerequisites. Reject for ZAP: mandatory human decisions on every paragraph. Documentation may change the order and form of explanation while preserving exact requirements and evidence.

p.ANCILLARY-GIT-GUARDRAILS: skills/misc/git-guardrails-claude-code/SKILL.md, lines 8–18, 24, 48, 81, 85, 89–95. Adapt: check authorization before an external effect and explicitly constrain configuration scope. Reject: treating a Bash hook as ZAP's complete authority boundary or automatically prohibiting every push. The hook script itself was not read in this pass and interception completeness was not established; the one negative example does not prove it. Verification should cover the actual surface of the specific control adapter.

p.ANCILLARY-SHOEHORN: skills/misc/migrate-to-shoehorn/SKILL.md, lines 12, 81–103, 107–118. Adapt: intentionally incomplete or incorrect data belongs explicitly to a test scenario. Reject for the ZAP methodology kernel: a particular library dependency, mechanical replacement of casts, and typecheck as sufficient behavioral proof. A fixture without material fields may produce an unrepresentative green result. There is no new principle here beyond explicit negative cases.

p.ANCILLARY-EXERCISES: skills/misc/scaffold-exercises/SKILL.md, lines 8, 19–31, 42, 46–50, 54–63, 69. Adapt: a scaffold has its own structural contract. Reject: treating file presence, a nonempty title, or a successful lint as proof of substantive readiness. Directory names and teaching tooling belong to another product. For ZAP this usefully illustrates the need to distinguish a created scaffold, a completed task, and an accepted obligation.

p.ANCILLARY-PRE-COMMIT: skills/misc/setup-pre-commit/SKILL.md, lines 19, 41–47, 53, 75–85, 91. Reject as the ZAP default: a full typecheck and all tests on every commit recreate the time loss identified by the Owner. Adapt when specifically needed: a cheap check of changed content that respects existing project commands. Automatic formatting of staged files changes the subject under test and requires corresponding evidence rebinding.

p.ANCILLARY-TEACH: skills/productivity/teach/SKILL.md, lines 14–18, 34–45, 53, 73–79, 93–108, 116–126. Adapt for documentation: connect the explanation to the reader's goal, provide a small verifiable result, and separate a concise reference from a step-by-step tutorial. Do not carry into the ZAP kernel: the teaching taxonomy, a mandatory external community, or prohibition of all model knowledge. The source's psychological claims were not independently verified. Verbal understanding does not replace a proven work result.

p.ANCILLARY-READER-PREREQUISITES: Viewer explanations and migration documentation may explicitly account for the reader's prior knowledge and introduce required concepts before using them. This improves presentation; it does not change the mandate, evidence graph, or execution rules.

p.ANCILLARY-CHECKER-FIXTURES: When creating a new checker, it is useful to test it with separate valid and invalid fixtures and exact expected results. This verifies the mechanism's ability to detect the stated defect. It does not introduce a mandatory mutation campaign or expand the verification scope of an ordinary change.

p.ANCILLARY-SETUP-REPEAT: A future setup adapter should be tested for repeated execution, preservation of existing settings, and absence of duplicate insertions. The test covers the actual configuration of the specific host. It is not grounds to install external skills or hooks now.

p.ANCILLARY-LIMIT: The remaining reviewed techniques are already reflected in ZAP, belong to other tasks, or conflict with the chosen autonomy and verification economy. This appendix supplements the primary research review while preserving its structure and twenty main ideas; it creates no new mandatory campaign phase.
